The [connected PR](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/51898) has been closed.

We still facing this issue in **8.0.3**, so we have to use the proposed workaround `app.UseExceptionHandler(o => {});`

Could you please reopen this issue?

Yes, we never ended up addressing this because the ramifications of the breaking change weren't fully enumerated.

I'll reopen this issue but considering the current prioritizations and the fact that there is a workaround, this will likely go in the backlog.

I'm open to reviewing a PR with a fix though!

fyi, I managed to get this issue on a brand new NET 8.0.8 Blazor Web Application project because I was calling this again by accident in a start-up helper function but without any parameters like so:
`app.UseExceptionHandler();`

I have this prior in the program.cs
` app.UseExceptionHandler("/Error", createScopeForErrors: true);`

The lack of parameters isn't an issue - it was the calling it twice!

For what i understand I can agree with @ghhv saying that the problem is how we configure the webApp, and not in the method itself.

I was having the same problem, and I was thinking I'd solved it with: `app.UseExceptionHandler(()=>{});` but, actually, we'd just bypassed the correct exception management.

The real problem seems that you need to register a "default" response in case your `IExceptionHandler` return `false` (Even if every exception is correctly managed inside the `IExceptionHandler`).

Actually adding 'AddProblemDetails()' before your exception handler seems doing the trick:

```
        builder.Services.AddProblemDetails();
        builder.Services.AddExceptionHandler<GlobalExceptionHandler>();
[...]
        var app = builder.Build();
        app.UseExceptionHandler();
```
 but i'm not sure is the correct behaviour.
I [leave here microsoft link with the method explanation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/web-api/handle-errors?view=aspnetcore-8.0):
 

> [...] code configures the app to generate a problem details response for all HTTP client and server error responses that don't have body content yet[...]
Hi, Any updates on this Fix ?

> Hi, Any updates on this Fix ?

Based on my understanding of the problem, my previous answer is a full fledged solution (at least until you hit [that other bug](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/47978)).
that problem is more a lack of documentation than an actual bug...
We were waiting confirmation from someone of the dev team if there is a more "clean" implementation... but at least we can consider it an acceptable alternative solution.

review_comments: Uhmm, Is this a breaking change!? I might want to handle some exceptions with `IExceptionHandler` and if they couldn't handle them, I want to execute the pipeline again. (`_options.ExceptionHandler = _next;`)
I don't know whether it was intended to work that way, but it certainly appears to, so changing it feels wrong.

> I might want to handle some exceptions with IExceptionHandler and if they couldn't handle them, I want to execute the pipeline again.

Is this supported at the moment (sans this change)?

There's a bit of a mess right now where an exception could be handled in one of three ways, an exception handler, problem details, or a delegate (e.g. re-execute). I tried to reconcile problem details and exception handlers but it was too breaking.
I don't understand why we'd ever set `_options.ExceptionHandler = _next`.  Isn't `_next` the thing that might throw, necessitating handling?
It looks like the only consumer does a null check first, so it's not to guarantee a non-null value.
It's set to _next when we also re-write the path and re-route the request to something that should be able to handle the exception.

Sorry, I'm not following.  It looks like `_next` is invoked first thing in `Invoke` and all the handling is downstream.  Doesn't that mean `_next` has already been invoked by the time `_options.ExceptionHandler` has been invoked?  Maybe you're saying that we rewrite the path _after_ the exception and then intentionally invoke `_next` _again_?

Yes :-)
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/b71c6d0295341ec354fe44d24f31de3f6fb79e2e/src/Middleware/Diagnostics/src/ExceptionHandler/ExceptionHandlerMiddlewareImpl.cs#L142-L187
That seems like the right place to update the handler?
? The Options shouldn't be modified after the constructor.
If that's the convention, then fair enough.

There's still an issue if this returns false. It will fall through to the IOE on line 217/222 and give the incorrect error about a 404. I think if problem details can't handle the error then we need to at least produce a different error.
Is there some way we can move this into the ctor?  Error handling seems like a really unfortunate place to report misconfiguration.
Oh, based on the thread with @Tratcher, maybe this just needs a better exception message?  I'm also curious about how the exception actually manifests.
This gets caught below and logged, then the original exception is re-thrown. The server catches it and produces a blank 500.

I placed it here because we only hit this situation if the exception handlers were not able to successfully process the exception. You don't necessarily run into this issue unless that's the case so if we were to move it to the constructor we would want a lower-severity notification to the user.

What if TryHandleAsync returns false and there's no ExceptionHandler configured? I don't think the middleware is expecting that.

I think you end up in problem details which is also optional.

Ah good point! I'm incline to say that in that case we throw an `InvalidOperationException` to be caught and logged here: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/Middleware/Diagnostics/src/ExceptionHandler/ExceptionHandlerMiddlewareImpl.cs#L224
Sure
